native_result.query: In the PCA conducted on forms of capital, analyzed in hundred-year time slices, how are the symbolic capital components such as house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords characterized in terms of their values on the first principal component (PC1) and distribution across the second principal component (PC2)?
native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the hundred-year-binned PCA of the 12 forms of capital (correlation matrix, re-standardized; PC1=30.3%, PC2=19.5%), the symbolic components (house size, daggers, hatchets/swords) load positively and moderately on PC1 (+0.23/+0.27/+0.30), sharing the same pole as copper/gold, hoards, pottery decoration and monument size — i.e., they ride the dominant wealth/prestige gradient. Along PC2 they split: house size carries a distinct positive loading (~+0.33) and defines the second-axis contrast, while daggers (~+0.07) and hatchets/swords (~+0.05) have near-zero PC2 loadings and are essentially PC1-aligned. The 39 bins follow an ordered neolithic->bronze-age trajectory on PC1 (EN negative to OBA positive) with a secondary MN-high/YBA-low contrast on PC2. A robustness check on the interpolated time series binned to 100y reproduces the same magnitudes and PC2 pattern (only the arbitrary PC1 sign flips).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/capital.csv (decimal=','; 39 rows, BCE 500-4300 step 100, 0 NAs), dropped group/color, took the 12 Z-capital variables, re-standardized (mean 0, unit variance), computed the Pearson correlation matrix, performed eigendecomposition (numpy.linalg.eigh), sorted by eigenvalue, fixed each PC sign so the largest-|loading| is positive, and read off PC1/PC2 loadings and period-grouped scores. Robustness: binned data/time_series_data.csv *_inter columns to 100y by BCE=-CE (groupby mean) and repeated the same PCA.
